'''Ivica Puljak''' (born 27 August 1969) is a Croatian politician, [[Particle physics|particle physicist]] and professor at [[University of Split]]'s [[Faculty of Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering and Naval Architecture, University of Split|FESB]] division. He served as [[List of mayors of Split|mayor of Split]] from 2021 to 2025 and was the president of the [[Centre (Croatian political party)|Centre]] political party.

== Life ==

=== Early life and education ===
Puljak was born in 1969 in [[Split, Croatia|Split]], [[Socialist Republic of Croatia|SR Croatia]], [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]]. His parents are from the [[Dalmatian Hinterland]] with his father, Zdravko, being from [[Zagvozd]] and mother, Jaka, from [[Drniš]].<ref name="Slobodna Dalmacija">{{cite web|url=https://slobodnadalmacija.hr/split/tezak-je-bio-put-od-ulice-do-bozje-cestice-ivica-puljak-prisjeca-se-zivota-bez-politike-odrastao-je-u-siromasnoj-igrao-za-juniore-hajduka-svirao-gitaru-1086446|title=Težak je bio put od ulice do 'Božje čestice': Ivica Puljak prisjeća se života bez politike. Odrastao je u 'Siromašnoj', igrao za juniore Hajduka, svirao gitaru...|date=24 March 2021|language=hr |access-date=26 August 2022}}</ref> Growing up in Split and attending primary and high school in his hometown, he dreamed of becoming a footballer for the local club, [[HNK Hajduk Split|Hajduk]].<ref name="Biografija">{{cite web|url=https://www.biografija.com/ivica-puljak/|title=Ivica Puljak biografija|date=8 May 2019|language=hr|access-date=26 August 2022}}</ref>

=== Personal life ===
Puljak is married to [[Marijana Puljak|Marijana Rakuljić]],<ref name="rakuljic">{{Cite web |date=2014-03-26 |title=Pametni ljudi za pametan grad |url=https://www.dugirat.com/novosti/120-lokalna-uprava/19021-pametni-ljudi-za-pametan-grad |access-date=2024-11-16 |website=Dugi Rat Online |language=hr}}</ref> the founder of [[Centre (Croatian political party)|Pametno]] and a [[Croatian Parliament|member of Croatian Parliament]]. They have two daughters and a son together.<ref name="Slobodna Dalmacija"></ref> He is an atheist.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Puljkov ‘urbi et orbi’. Premijeru objasnio zašto više nije vjernik: “To sam priznao prvo sebi, a onda…” |url=https://www.nacional.hr/puljkov-urbi-et-orbi-premijeru-objasnio-zasto-vise-nije-vjernik-to-sam-priznao-prvo-sebi-a-onda/ |work=Nacional.hr |language=Croatian}}</ref>

== Scientific career ==
He has been working for his PhD thesis at Laboratory Leprince Ringuet (LLR) at [[Ecole Polytechnique]], [[Palaiseau]], and got his PhD on  search for [[Higgs boson]] from [[Pierre and Marie Curie University|University Paris VI]] in 2000 for which he was awarded the best CMS thesis award in 2001. He is a member of [[Compact Muon Solenoid|CMS collaboration]] since 1994 and [[MAGIC (telescope)|MAGIC collaboration]] since 2009. He was a co-coordinator of more than a hundred scientists from all over the world working on the most sensitive and precise of all physical processes through which the Higgs boson was discovered and measured. His research interests are the construction of the electromagnetic calorimeter of the CMS detector, development and implementation of algorithms for the electron reconstruction of the CMS detector, physics of the Higgs boson and astroparticle physics. He was awarded the Annual Award for Science in 2013.<ref name="Biografija"></ref><ref name="Jutarnji List">{{cite web|url=https://www.jutarnji.hr/life/znanost/video-pronasli-smo-bozju-cesticu-na-objavi-otkrica-peter-higgs-nije-mogao-zaustaviti-suze-1537872|title=NAJVAŽNIJE ZNANSTVENO OTKRIĆE U POVIJESTI VIDEO Pronašli smo Božju česticu: Na objavi otkrića Peter Higgs nije mogao zaustaviti suze|date=4 July 2012|language=hr|access-date=26 August 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Ivica Puljak, Assistant Professor in the Technical University of Split in Croatia receives the award for the best CMS thesis 2001 | url =https://cds.cern.ch/search?f=keyword&p=CMS%20Awards%20Thesis&ln=hr}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title= Prof. Ivica Puljak Winner of the Annual Award For Science in the Field of Natural Sciences (translation) | url= https://www.fesb.unist.hr/2014/07/18/prof-dr-sc-ivica-puljak-dobitnik-godisnje-nagrade-za-znanost-u-podrucju-prirodnih-znanosti/ }}</ref>

== Political career ==
Puljak ran for and won the [[2021 Split local elections|2021 Split mayoral elections]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Splitsko-dalmatinska županija - Split - Gradonačelnik / Općinski načelnik - Stanje od 17.05.2021 u 13:00 |url=https://www.izbori.hr/lokalni2021/rezultati/1/ |publisher=State Election Committee of Croatia |access-date=17 May 2021 |language=hr |date=17 May 2021 |archive-date=16 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210516190216/https://www.izbori.hr/lokalni2021/rezultati/1/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
After about one year, a special election was summoned due to the dissolution of the city council, where Puljak had lost his majority. Adding to the commotion, his deputy mayor, Bojan Ivošević, was charged with threatening a journalist.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Maretić Žonja |first1=Petra |last2=Filipović |first2=Juraj |date=30 March 2022 |title=Doznajemo! Puljak i Ivošević daju ostavke, Split ide na nove izbore! |trans-title=We find out! Puljak and Ivošević resign, Split goes to new elections! |url=https://www.vecernji.hr/vijesti/gotovo-je-sigurno-da-split-ide-na-nove-izbore-puljak-je-prelomio-ali-ostaje-jedna-nepoznanica-1574959 |access-date=15 March 2022 |website=Večernji list |language=hr}}</ref> On 8 April, Mayor Puljak and both his deputies resigned.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 April 2022 |title=Gradonačelnik Puljak i zamjenik Ivošević podnijeli ostavke, a neočekivano im se pridružio i Kuzmanić |trans-title=Mayor Puljak and Deputy Ivošević resigned, and Kuzmanić unexpectedly joined them |url=https://www.jutarnji.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/gradonacelnik-puljak-i-zamjenik-ivosevic-podnijeli-ostavke-a-neocekivano-im-se-pridruzio-i-kuzmanic-15181401 |access-date=15 April 2022 |website=Jutarnji list |language=hr}}</ref> Ivica Puljak won [[2022 Split local elections|the special election]] becoming the first mayor of Split to win more than one election and his party [[Centre (Croatian political party)|Centre]] won 15 seats out of 31 in the city council.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 July 2022 |title=Ivica Puljak nakon uvjerljive pobjede: "Bit ću gradonačelnik svih građana Splita. Učinit ćemo da Split bude centar regije" |trans-title=Ivica Puljak after a convincing victory: "I will be the mayor of all the citizens of Split. We will make Split the center of the region" |url=https://dnevnik.hr/vijesti/hrvatska/ivica-puljak-nakon-objave-prvih-nesluzbenih-rezultata-izbora---732475.html?itm_source=HomeTopRow&itm_medium=Dnevnik&itm_campaign=Naslovnica |access-date=10 July 2022 |website=Dnevnik.hr |language=hr}}</ref> On 18 May 2025, he won a plurality of 4,72% of votes; in the runoff election he won 46,81% of the votes, losing to HDZ's Tomislav Šuta. Upon losing the re-election, Puljak announced that he will retire from politics and resume his scientific career.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Razmjeri Puljkova izbornog fijaska: u Splitu dobio manje glasova od svoje uzdanice |url=https://www.telegram.hr/politika-kriminal/razmjeri-puljkova-izbornog-fijaska-u-splitu-dobio-manje-glasova-od-svoje-uzdanice/ |last=Vranješ |first=Mirta |date=2025-06-02 |access-date=2025-06-04 |website=Telegram}}</ref>
